mechanism_narrative: The persistent four-week decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility reflects reduced commuting and discretionary trips, which suppresses footfall at retail and recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC remains lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below their last-28-day means.

mechanism_narrative: When the weekly mean WORKPLACES mobility falls below -40 percent, workplace attendance restrictions are binding and weekday retail traffic drops further, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the prior 14 days in more than half of observed instances where WORKPLACES fell below -40.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility and depressed WORKPLACES mobility indicates widespread stay-at-home behavior, which reduces non-essential retail trips and keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean > 10 and WORKPLACES weekly mean < -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days when RESIDENTIAL > 10 and WORKPLACES < -40.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, a week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 10 points signals newly imposed mobility limits that also cut retail visits, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the prior 14 days when TRANSIT fell by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility rises above -10 percent, it signals a relaxation of outdoor restrictions and a broader reopening that boosts discretionary retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days when PARKS rose above -10.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility relative to depressed RETAIL_REC indicates households are limiting shopping to essentials, so retail traffic stays weak and RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than over the last 7 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains within 3 points of its last-4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: The seasonal transition from late winter to early spring in Sydney raises outdoor activity, and rising PARKS mobility pulls shoppers back to retail districts, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite PARKS rising above -10.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall sharply in the same week, it signals a compliance shock to movement restrictions, and the resulting drop in retail footfall lowers RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls >10 points and WORKPLACES falls >10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than over the last 7 days when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fell more than 10 points week-on-week.
